heuristics.rule: Plan B should be prepared before the third H-1B lottery attempt, not after
heuristics.condition: When an F-1 student is in STEM OPT and has already failed 1-2 H-1B lotteries...
heuristics.action: Begin actively researching and preparing alternative paths (O-1, Canada, cap-exempt employers, NIW) during OPT, not after the third failure
heuristics.because: STEM OPT gives 3 lottery chances; the probability of failing all three is 25-30%, which is high enough to warrant concurrent preparation rather than sequential hoping

heuristics.rule: Cap-exempt employer + concurrent employment is a structurally valid workaround for H-1B lottery
heuristics.condition: When a person wants to work at a private company but cannot clear the H-1B cap...
heuristics.action: Arrange part-time researcher role at a university or nonprofit research institution (which files a cap-exempt H-1B petition) while working full-time at the private company under concurrent employment
heuristics.because: Universities, nonprofit research institutions, and government research organizations are exempt from H-1B numerical caps and can file petitions year-round; concurrent employment under this structure is legal but requires attorney-designed setup

heuristics.rule: O-1A is a viable alternative for STEM professionals with documented achievements, not just celebrities
heuristics.condition: When a person has accumulated peer-review authorship, citations, awards, media coverage, or high relative compensation in their field...
heuristics.action: Evaluate O-1A petition viability with an immigration attorney, as it bypasses the H-1B lottery entirely
heuristics.because: O-1A has no cap or lottery; community commenters with upvotes confirm people in tech have successfully used this path after building a record of accomplishment

heuristics.rule: EB-2 NIW is a self-petition path worth evaluating for STEM graduates before assuming employer sponsorship is the only route
heuristics.condition: When a STEM-background international student is considering long-term US stay and has an employer or research background...
heuristics.action: Research the Matter of Dhanasar three-prong test to self-assess NIW eligibility; consult an attorney before dismissing it as too difficult
heuristics.because: Multiple high-upvote comments confirm the NIW threshold is lower than commonly assumed, and it does not require employer sponsorship

decision_factors.why_it_matters: TN visa is exclusively available to Canadian and Mexican citizens, offering a cap-free, attorney-optional path for qualifying professional occupations — a major structural advantage unavailable to Chinese or Indian nationals
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm passport country; verify target job title appears on TN qualifying occupations list (engineers, scientists qualify)

decision_factors.factor: Whether current or prospective employer is cap-exempt
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Cap-exempt employers (universities, nonprofit research institutions, government research orgs) can file H-1B petitions at any time without entering the lottery, fundamentally changing the H-1B access pathway
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask employer's HR or immigration counsel whether the organization qualifies as cap-exempt; check if the role is primarily research-based at a qualifying institution

decision_factors.factor: Strength of professional record for O-1A or EB-1A
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The higher the documented achievement (citations, awards, peer review, high relative salary), the more viable the lottery-free O-1A or direct EB-1A green card path becomes — shifting the decision calculus away from H-1B dependency
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Conduct an O-1A self-audit: count qualifying criteria met (USCIS requires at least 3 of 8); consult an attorney for realistic assessment

decision_factors.factor: Whether the person's employer is a multinational with overseas offices
decision_factors.why_it_matters: L-1 intracompany transferee visa requires prior employment at a foreign affiliate; if the employer has no overseas presence, this path is unavailable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm employer has qualifying foreign parent, subsidiary, or affiliate; verify willingness to employ person overseas for 1+ year before transfer

decision_factors.factor: Tolerance for geographic relocation (US vs. Canada)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canada's Express Entry and PGWP represent a structurally different immigration system — points-based, more predictable, and with open work permits — but requires accepting a different country as the destination
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate personal ties, career market, salary expectations, and long-term settlement goals in Canada vs. continuing to pursue US options

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Pursuing cap-exempt H-1B via university concurrent employment structure
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: This arrangement requires careful legal design — the university role must be genuine and substantive enough to qualify as cap-exempt employment, not a paper arrangement; improper structuring can constitute immigration fraud
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: People who attempt to set up this structure informally or without proper legal counsel

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Waiting through all three STEM OPT lottery cycles before planning alternatives
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: By the time the third lottery failure occurs, the person has 60 days to change status or leave; there is no runway left to build an O-1A record, set up L-1 overseas employment, or transition to Canada with PGWP eligibility
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: STEM OPT holders who treat lottery failures sequentially rather than planning alternatives in parallel

hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: L-1B (specialized knowledge) has a high denial rate and is subject to RFE scrutiny; L-1A (managerial/executive) is stronger but requires genuinely managerial responsibilities — many people discover their overseas role does not qualify after spending 1+ year abroad
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Mid-level individual contributors who assume their technical role qualifies as 'specialized knowledge' without attorney assessment

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Switching focus to Canada after multiple H-1B failures
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: PGWP is only available to people who studied in Canada; those who only studied in the US must enter Canada via employer-sponsored work permit or Express Entry, which has its own processing time and uncertainty — it is not an immediate fallback
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: US-educated international students who assume Canada is a simple pivot without understanding that PGWP eligibility requires Canadian study

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating each H-1B lottery failure as a one-year delay rather than a signal to activate alternative plans
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Status quo bias and optimism bias: after each failure, it feels rational to 'just try again next year' because the cost of switching strategies feels higher than the cost of waiting one more year
failure_patterns.consequence: By the third failure, the person has no time to build O-1A credentials, pursue L-1 overseas positioning, or transition to Canada with enough runway; they face a forced departure instead of a planned pivot
warning_signs: Person says 'I'll figure it out if I don't get it this year' after the first or second failure
No concrete Plan B exists after the first lottery loss
Person is unfamiliar with O-1A, NIW, or cap-exempt employer options despite 2 years into STEM OPT

failure_patterns.pattern: Dismissing EB-2 NIW as 'too hard' without actually assessing eligibility under Matter of Dhanasar
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: NIW sounds like an elite path (national interest, extraordinary contribution) which primes people to self-exclude; the Dhanasar three-prong standard is less known than the colloquial reputation
failure_patterns.consequence: STEM professionals who would have qualified for self-petition NIW continue chasing employer-sponsored H-1B or assume they have no path, when a more stable route was available
warning_signs: Person says 'NIW is only for famous scientists' or 'I'm not important enough for that'
Person has never read or heard of the Dhanasar standard
Person is a STEM PhD or postdoc with publications but has never discussed NIW with an attorney

diagnostic_questions.question: Is your current or target employer a university, nonprofit research institution, or government research organization?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Cap-exempt status — if yes, H-1B can be filed year-round without lottery, fundamentally changing the entire strategy
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does the role qualify as H-1B specialty occupation? Is concurrent employment with a private company also desired?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Does the employer have overseas offices where you could work for 1+ year to enable an L-1 petition?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you hold Canadian or Mexican citizenship?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: TN visa eligibility — if yes, a cap-free, relatively simple work authorization path may exist for qualifying professional occupations
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does your job title appear on the TN qualifying occupations list?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Eliminate TN from consideration; focus on O-1, cap-exempt H-1B, L-1, NIW, or Canada immigration

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you published peer-reviewed work, been cited, reviewed others' papers, received awards, or been reported on by media in your field?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: O-1A and EB-1A viability — each of these counts as one of the eight USCIS O-1A criteria; meeting three or more makes O-1A worth a serious attorney consultation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Get an O-1A credential audit from an immigration attorney; simultaneously assess EB-1A for a direct green card path
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Can any of these be built in the next 12-24 months (conference presentations, peer review invitations, etc.) to create a future O-1A pathway?

diagnostic_questions.question: How many H-1B lottery attempts do you have remaining under your current STEM OPT authorization?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Time pressure and runway — one attempt remaining means this is the last cycle; the person should have a fully prepared alternative plan already in place, not just under consideration
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If one attempt remains: has a concrete Plan B (O-1, L-1 positioning, Canada, NIW) already been initiated?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If multiple attempts remain: start building O-1A credentials and researching alternatives now, not after the next failure

industry_realities.common_belief: If you fail H-1B three times, your only options are to give up on the US or go back home
industry_realities.actual_reality: Multiple lottery-free legal paths exist: cap-exempt H-1B (via university/nonprofit employers), O-1A (extraordinary ability), L-1 (intracompany transfer), EB-1A (extraordinary ability green card), EB-2 NIW (self-petition), and TN for Canadian/Mexican citizens — each with different eligibility criteria
industry_realities.implication: Students should map their eligibility across all these paths early in OPT, not treat them as emergency options discovered after the third failure

industry_realities.common_belief: The H-1B lottery is the primary or only standard path to long-term US work authorization for international students
industry_realities.actual_reality: The H-1B lottery has a roughly 25-30% chance of failing across all three STEM OPT attempts; experienced community members treat it as one path among many, not THE path, and begin parallel preparation from the start
industry_realities.implication: Framing H-1B as the default creates fragility; treating it as one option among a portfolio creates resilience

industry_realities.common_belief: EB-2 NIW requires extraordinary national-level contributions and is effectively only available to senior scientists or famous researchers
industry_realities.actual_reality: The Matter of Dhanasar (2016) three-prong standard is more accessible than the colloquial reputation suggests; multiple community commenters with high upvotes confirm that STEM-background students with solid but not exceptional records have qualified
industry_realities.implication: STEM graduates — especially PhDs and researchers — should assess NIW eligibility early rather than defaulting to employer-sponsored H-1B as the only green card route

industry_realities.common_belief: Canada is a fallback or consolation prize for those who fail to stay in the US
industry_realities.actual_reality: Multiple high-upvote comments frame Canada's Express Entry as structurally superior in predictability: CRS points system is transparent, PGWP is an open work permit (no visa anxiety when changing jobs), and PR timelines of 2-3 years are realistic — not a degraded outcome
industry_realities.implication: Reframing Canada as a parallel strategic option rather than a fallback changes how early and seriously people engage with it, potentially yielding better outcomes

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Treats each failure as a one-year setback; waits passively for the next lottery window; does not initiate alternatives until forced
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: After the first or second failure, immediately audits eligibility for O-1A, NIW, cap-exempt employers, and L-1; begins building credentials or positioning concurrently with the next lottery attempt
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: By the time of the third failure, someone with the informed pattern has options ready; someone with the naive pattern faces a 60-day departure deadline with no alternatives prepared

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Knows H-1B and vaguely knows O-1 exists; treats them as exotic or inaccessible; assumes there is no path if H-1B fails
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Can name and roughly assess cap-exempt H-1B, O-1A, EB-1A, EB-2 NIW, L-1, TN, and Canada Express Entry; knows which apply based on their own profile
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Knowledge of the full option set is a prerequisite for making a rational plan; ignorance of alternatives creates false binary (H-1B or leave)

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: View of Canada as an immigration destination
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Views Canada as a last resort or inferior outcome; only considers it after US options are exhausted
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Evaluates Canada as a parallel track with distinct structural advantages (open work permit, points-based predictability, 2-3 year PR timeline); some proactively choose it over continued H-1B lottery exposure
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Late consideration of Canada means less runway to establish qualifying work experience or Canadian study history; early consideration preserves more options

community_misconceptions.misconception: PGWP is an option for US-educated international students who want to move to Canada after H-1B failures
community_misconceptions.why_believed: PGWP is Canada's post-graduation work permit and sounds like it should be available to any international graduate; it is prominently mentioned as a Canada pathway, leading US-educated students to assume they qualify
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: PGWP is only available to international students who graduated from a designated learning institution (DLI) in Canada; US-educated graduates are not eligible and must enter Canada via employer-sponsored work permit or Express Entry
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: A US-educated student who plans to 'just go to Canada and get PGWP' will find this path closed; they need a different entry strategy (Express Entry with job offer, provincial nomination, or employer LMIA-based sponsorship)

community_misconceptions.misconception: The cap-exempt H-1B via university concurrent employment is a simple, low-risk workaround anyone can set up
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The best answer describes it as 'legal' and explains the logic clearly, which makes it sound straightforward; the caveat that it requires attorney-designed structure is present but easy to underweight
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: The university role must be substantive and genuine to qualify as cap-exempt employment; a paper or token appointment may not satisfy USCIS; the structure requires proper legal design and carries risk if improperly set up
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: An improperly structured arrangement could constitute immigration fraud or result in denial of the H-1B petition; people who try to replicate this without legal counsel may create serious legal exposure

community_misconceptions.misconception: Three H-1B lottery failures effectively means you cannot stay in the US legally long-term
community_misconceptions.why_believed: H-1B is by far the most commonly discussed path in student communities; when it fails repeatedly, it feels like the main door is closed, and alternatives are either unknown or feel inaccessible
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Multiple cap-free and lottery-free paths exist (O-1A, EB-1A, EB-2 NIW, L-1, TN, cap-exempt H-1B) with different eligibility requirements; three lottery failures do not foreclose legal long-term presence
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: People who believe this misconception may leave the US prematurely or fail to pursue paths they actually qualify for, resulting in unnecessary departure

real_case_outcomes.situation: International student or worker failed H-1B lottery multiple times and sought an alternative path to remain in the US
real_case_outcomes.decision: Arranged a part-time researcher role at a university (cap-exempt employer) while maintaining full-time employment at a private company under concurrent employment; university filed an H-1B petition outside the lottery
real_case_outcomes.outcome: H-1B approved through cap-exempt channel without lottery participation; person continued working at private company
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Cap-exempt concurrent employment is a real and documented workaround for the H-1B lottery, but requires attorney-designed structure and a genuine qualifying university role — not a self-executable hack

real_case_outcomes.situation: Multiple H-1B lottery failures after STEM OPT; person reassessed options and pivoted to Canada
real_case_outcomes.decision: Pursued Canadian immigration via Express Entry or employer sponsorship rather than continuing to wait for H-1B
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Canadian PR obtained within 2-3 years; person established stable immigration status with open work permit during the process
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Canada Express Entry provides a predictable, transparent PR pathway that multiple people in this situation have successfully used within 2-3 years; it is not a consolation prize but a legitimate parallel strategy

psychological_barriers.trigger: Person has failed H-1B twice and is asking 'what are my options if I fail again?' — but framed as a hypothetical rather than an active planning question
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Magical thinking and deferral: asking about options as a theoretical exercise rather than actually initiating alternatives, because initiating them feels like admitting defeat on H-1B
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Person researches alternatives intellectually but takes no concrete preparatory action; says 'I'll look into that if it comes to it'; does not consult an attorney or apply to cap-exempt jobs
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: 'The question isn't whether you believe you'll get it next year — the question is what it costs you to start Plan B now vs. what it costs you if you need it and haven't started. The asymmetry is obvious.'

psychological_barriers.trigger: Person describes Canada or O-1 as 'not for me' or 'I'm not at that level' without any factual assessment of their eligibility
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Defensive pessimism masking avoidance: dismissing alternatives preemptively so that not pursuing them feels like a choice rather than a failure to try
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Categorical self-exclusion from paths not yet properly evaluated; reliance on reputation ('NIW is only for famous people') rather than actual eligibility criteria
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Ask the person to name the actual standard — 'What are the three Dhanasar prongs? What are the eight O-1A criteria? Let's go through them for your profile before you decide it doesn't apply to you.'

psychological_barriers.trigger: Person who has failed two H-1B lotteries is intensely focused on the third attempt — researching lottery timing, registration details, and employer willingness — while not mentioning any alternative planning
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost and tunnel vision: each lottery attempt invested time, employer goodwill, and emotional energy; the more attempts made, the harder it is to redirect attention to alternatives
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: All cognitive and practical energy directed at maximizing the next lottery attempt; alternatives treated as distractions rather than parallel priorities
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Normalize parallel planning: 'Preparing a strong alternative does not reduce your lottery odds. You can do both. The only risk is doing only one.'

reframing_moves.original_framing: What do I do if I fail H-1B three times? (Framed as a crisis or endpoint)
reframing_moves.reframe: Three failures is a predictable outcome for roughly 25-30% of people — it is a known risk, not a surprise, and has a known set of responses that should be prepared in advance
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts from reactive crisis management to proactive risk management; replaces the emotional framing of 'failure' with a probabilistic framing of 'expected outcome requiring parallel preparation'
reframing_moves.example_language: '做好这个心理预期，早早准备Plan B，不是认输，是理性规划。' (Having this psychological expectation and preparing Plan B early is not giving up — it is rational planning.)

reframing_moves.original_framing: Canada is the fallback for people who couldn't make it in the US
reframing_moves.reframe: Canada's immigration system is structurally more predictable and transparent than the US H-1B lottery system; choosing it proactively is a rational optimization, not a consolation
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Removes the status hierarchy framing (US = success, Canada = failure) and replaces it with a systems comparison framing; enables the person to evaluate Canada on its actual merits rather than as an ego threat
reframing_moves.example_language: '加拿大这条路值得认真研究，不是退而求其次。' (The Canada path is worth serious research — it is not settling for less.)
